items.title: Anthropic to commit 5% of its shares to new public benefit fund ahead of IPO, pending stockholder approval
items.summary: Anthropic announced it will set aside 5% of its shares for a new public benefit fund structured as a wholly owned LLC, subject to stockholder approval. The stake could grow by an extra 2% at the board's discretion for each 50% rise in company value above an undisclosed baseline. Reuters reports that, counting earlier pledges, roughly 20% of shares would be dedicated to public-purpose uses; Bloomberg frames the fund as a vehicle for donations including mitigating AI's labour-market effects. Anthropic has not named recipients or said how stock would be converted to cash.
items.why_it_matters: An unusually large equity pledge by an AI lab weeks before an expected IPO could shape governance, dilution and public scrutiny of the listing.
key_numbers: ~20% of shares for public good incl. earlier pledges

items.title: Microsoft pulls out of Nscale's Loughton UK data centre deal, Telegraph reports; grid power not expected until 2030s
items.summary: The Telegraph reported, and Reuters and Bloomberg relayed, that Microsoft has withdrawn from its planned anchor-tenant deal for Nscale's data centre in Loughton, Essex. Grid officials had reportedly told Nscale not to expect power until the 2030s. Nscale said its Microsoft relationship 'remains strong' and that it is exploring alternative power for the site. Microsoft declined to comment. Nscale's IPO filing reportedly shows Microsoft and Anthropic make up about 85% of its contracts, and it is seeking up to $3B in a US listing as soon as this month.
items.why_it_matters: A concrete case of grid constraints killing a hyperscale deal, hitting a neocloud just ahead of its IPO.

items.title: Samsung to use TSMC 3nm for base dies in Nvidia's next-gen custom HBM, Seoul Economic Daily reports
items.summary: Per Seoul Economic Daily via Reuters, Samsung will make base dies for Nvidia's next-generation custom HBM on TSMC's 3nm process, reportedly the first time Samsung has worked with TSMC at the HBM manufacturing stage. Nvidia reportedly asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use TSMC's process for base dies and sixth-generation DRAM for the core dies. Samsung reportedly accepted but will keep in-house base dies for standard HBM and other customers' custom parts, and is weighing its own foundry as overflow if TSMC capacity is short.
items.why_it_matters: Signals TSMC's growing grip on the HBM stack and a pragmatic Samsung-Nvidia accommodation in memory.

items.title: Anthropic report: junior share of technical staff fell from 21% to 14%; agents now outwork humans
items.summary: Anthropic's economics team published a study of its own workforce. Junior employees fell from 21% to 14% of technical staff, and juniors' share of technical hires fell from 27% to 9%. By March 2026 combined agent work hours passed human hours, and by August interactive agents logged about six times their handlers' hours. Commits per engineer were about 5x their level six months earlier, with no difference in later reverts among 192 adopters vs 74 non-adopters.
items.why_it_matters: A rare first-party dataset on how agentic coding reshapes a frontier lab's hiring and output, with human attention (about 80% of interactive session time spent waiting on people) as the main constraint.

items.title: DeepSeek details Search/Fetch API billing: 5 yuan per 1,000 successful calls, 5 requests/s cap
items.original_title: DeepSeek API 已支持网页搜索和抓取，单价为每 1000 次成功请求 5 元
items.summary: DeepSeek's API docs now carry a guide for web search and fetch, priced at 5 yuan (about $0.75) per 1,000 successful requests. Chinese outlets report a call is billed only if Search returns non-empty results or Fetch returns body text with HTTP 200, so failures and timeouts are free. Each account is limited to 5 queries per second per endpoint. Server-side tool calls from DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code or Codex are reportedly free until Beijing time Nov 1 00:00. The docs page drew 471 points on Hacker News.
items.why_it_matters: DeepSeek is moving from models into the agent tool stack, pricing search for coding agents including rival tools.

items.title: Anthropic's proposed federal AI safety bill reportedly only triggers at 50 deaths or $1B in damage
items.summary: Tom's Hardware, PC Gamer, Mother Jones and others highlight that the federal frontier-AI safety bill Anthropic pitched to Congress would reportedly give government power to act only at a threshold of 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages. Tom's Hardware's headline says this would effectively make the Commerce Department the only agency able to stop a model. The desk found the same 50-deaths/$1B line in California's SB 53, which Anthropic backed.
items.why_it_matters: Critics read the draft's trigger as too late to be preventive, shaping the congressional debate over federal AI preemption.

items.title: Anthropic consults lawyers on negotiation norms for AI agents that bargain with other agents, FT reports
items.summary: The FT reports Anthropic is consulting law firms on negotiation tactics as it builds agents that haggle over prices, resolve complaints and make contract offers against counterparties' AI agents. It is studying how human lawyers negotiate for clients and how much latitude agents should have, including when to seek guidance. Secondary summaries cite its internal Project Deal test, where 69 employees' Claude agents closed 186 deals worth just over $4,000 without human approval.
items.why_it_matters: Agent-to-agent commerce raises liability and fairness questions that will land in contract law and regulation.

items.title: Nvidia says first RTX Spark Windows laptops are arriving, with a Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU
items.summary: Nvidia's blog marked the arrival of the first RTX Spark Windows PCs. RTX Spark was unveiled May 31 at GTC Taipei and pairs a 20-core Grace Arm CPU (co-designed with MediaTek) with a Blackwell GPU of 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB unified memory. Nvidia claims it can run models up to 120B parameters locally. Partners include ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Surface and MSI.
items.why_it_matters: Nvidia's entry into Windows PC silicon targets local AI and agent workloads and competes with Intel and AMD.
